narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 53% chance you won’t pass your final year, which is well above the 10% threshold that requires extra support. Because of this, you’ll need to take remedial courses to help you stay on track.

The main reason the model reached this conclusion is that you’ve failed classes three times before. This history of struggling in school is the strongest signal that you’re at risk of falling behind again. On the other hand, two things are working in your favor: you’ve expressed a clear goal of pursuing higher education, and you didn’t attend nursery school. Both of these slightly reduce the likelihood of failing, but not enough to outweigh the concern raised by your past failures.

Other factors also played a role. For example, your parents have limited formal education, and you spend less than two hours a week studying—far below what most students who pass dedicate to their work. You also don’t have internet access at home, which can make it harder to complete assignments or research topics independently. While your family relationships are strong and you have support from home, these challenges make it more difficult to keep up.

The good news is that remedial courses are designed to help you catch up. Focus on using this opportunity to build better study habits, seek extra help when needed, and take advantage of the resources available to you. With effort, you can improve your chances of success.
